lesson.arabic-claim-evidence.title_en: Claims and evidence: اِدِّعَاء, دَلِيلٌ كَافٍ, تَعْمِيم
lesson.arabic-claim-evidence.family_en: What a writer claims, what supports it, and when one example becomes a generalisation

table.en: an argument, a reason offered as proof
he supported his view with an example

steps: A claim, اِدِّعَاء, is what the writer wants you to accept; evidence is what's offered to support it.
Test the evidence three ways: is it ذُو صِلَةٍ, relevant? Is it كَافٍ, enough? Does it cover more than one case?
One example can illustrate; turning it into a rule for everyone is a تَعْمِيم, a generalisation.
Keep apart whether you agree with the conclusion and how well it's supported.
ذُو, "having", changes with its noun's ending: دَلِيلٌ ذُو صِلَةٍ, but دَلِيلًا ذَا صِلَةٍ and بِدَلِيلٍ ذِي صِلَةٍ.

examples.ar: دَعَمَ الْكَاتِبُ رَأْيَهُ بِأَرْقَامٍ مِنْ ثَلَاثِ دِرَاسَاتٍ.
examples.en: The writer supported his view with figures from three studies.

examples.ar: هَذَا الْمِثَالُ وَحْدَهُ لَيْسَ دَلِيلًا كَافِيًا.
examples.en: This example alone isn't sufficient evidence.

examples.ar: الْحُجَّةُ مُقْنِعَةٌ، لَكِنَّهَا تَقُومُ عَلَى تَعْمِيمٍ.
examples.en: The argument is convincing, but it rests on a generalisation.

why.q_en: Why كَافٍ in دَلِيلٌ كَافٍ, but كَافِيًا in لَيْسَ دَلِيلًا كَافِيًا?
why.a_en: Words like كَافٍ end in a long ī that drops with -un and -in: كَافٍ. With -an the ي stays: كَافِيًا. It's the same with غَالٍ, غَالِيًا.

selftest.why_en: It turns one or a few cases into a rule for all.
دَلِيلٌ ends in -un, so ذُو. ذَا goes with -an, and ذِي with -in.

lesson.arabic-stance-hedging.title_en: How sure a claim is: بِالتَّأْكِيدِ, عَلَى الْأَرْجَحِ, يَبْدُو أَنَّ
lesson.arabic-stance-hedging.family_en: Words that set the strength of a claim, from certain to possible
steps: These words set how sure a claim is. They aren't decoration: change one and you change the claim.
From surest to least sure: بِالتَّأْكِيدِ, certainly; عَلَى الْأَرْجَحِ, most likely; مِنَ الْمُحْتَمَلِ أَنْ, it's likely that; رُبَّمَا, perhaps; لَا أَسْتَبْعِدُ, I don't rule it out.
Watch what follows: مِنَ الْمُحْتَمَلِ أَنْ takes a present verb ending in -a; يَبْدُو أَنَّ takes a noun ending in -a.
قَدْ with a present verb is "may": قَدْ يَتَأَخَّرُ الْقِطَارُ, the train may be late.
Keep the strength when you translate or summarise: don't make "most likely" into "certainly".

examples.ar: مِنَ الْمُحْتَمَلِ أَنْ تَنْخَفِضَ الْأَسْعَارُ قَلِيلًا.
examples.en: Prices are likely to fall slightly.
It seems the meeting has been postponed.

examples.ar: هَذِهِ الطَّرِيقَةُ مُفِيدَةٌ إِلَى حَدٍّ مَا.
examples.en: This method is useful to some extent.

why.q_en: Why أَنْ before a verb, but أَنَّ before a noun?
why.a_en: أَنْ brings in a verb, which then ends in -a: مِنَ الْمُحْتَمَلِ أَنْ تَنْخَفِضَ. أَنَّ, with a shadda, brings in a noun, which also ends in -a: يَبْدُو أَنَّ الِاجْتِمَاعَ تَأَجَّلَ.

selftest.why_en: The other two leave room for doubt.

selftest.q_en: What does إِلَى حَدٍّ مَا mean?
selftest.why_en: حَدّ is a limit: "up to some limit".
Before a noun it's أَنَّ, and the noun after it ends in -a.

lesson.arabic-implicit-meaning.title_en: What a text says and what it implies: صَرِيح, ضِمْنِيّ
lesson.arabic-implicit-meaning.family_en: Stated meaning, reasonable inference, and the small words that carry it

table.en: he suggested that, he hinted that

steps: Keep three levels apart: what the text says, صَرِيح; what it reasonably implies, ضِمْنِيّ; and what would only be a guess.
Small words often carry the implication: مَرَّةً أُخْرَى, again, implies it happened before; حَتَّى, even, implies surprise.
An implication isn't proof of someone's نِيَّة, intention: say the text suggests it, يُوحِي النَّصُّ بِأَنَّ, not that the writer meant it.
Back an interpretation with words from the text, and allow other readings when the text allows them.

examples.en: Even the teacher didn't know the answer.
The title suggests the article is critical.

why.q_en: What does حَتَّى add in حَتَّى الْمُعَلِّمُ لَمْ يَعْرِفِ الْجَوَابَ?
why.a_en: It implies you'd expect the teacher to know. The sentence never says so; حَتَّى, even, carries that surprise.

selftest.q_en: What does مَرَّةً أُخْرَى imply in تَعَطَّلَ الْمِصْعَدُ مَرَّةً أُخْرَى?
selftest.why_en: "Again" implies an earlier time; it says nothing about who or why.

selftest.q_en: What is the opposite of صَرِيح?
selftest.why_en: صَرِيح is stated; ضِمْنِيّ is implied.
It points to a meaning without stating it.

lesson.arabic-counterargument.title_en: Answering the other side: صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ, وَمَعَ ذَلِكَ
lesson.arabic-counterargument.family_en: Conceding a point fairly, then keeping your own
steps: Put the other view fairly, in its strongest form, before you answer it.
Concede what's true with صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ, then keep your point with مَعَ ذَلِكَ or لَكِنَّ: صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ السَّفَرَ مُكْلِفٌ، وَمَعَ ذَلِكَ فَهُوَ يُعَلِّمُ الْكَثِيرَ.
Answer the real reason, not a مُبَالَغَة, an exaggerated version of it.
Look for أَرْضِيَّةٌ مُشْتَرَكَةٌ, common ground, before you set out the difference.

examples.ar: صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ الْعَمَلَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ مُرِيحٌ، لَكِنَّهُ قَدْ يَعْزِلُ الْمُوَظَّفِينَ.
examples.en: It's true that working from home is comfortable, but it can isolate staff.

examples.ar: هَذَا اعْتِرَاضٌ وَجِيهٌ، وَمَعَ ذَلِكَ أَرَى الْأَمْرَ بِشَكْلٍ مُخْتَلِفٍ.
examples.en: That's a valid objection; even so, I see it differently.
The writer refuted the argument with figures.

why.q_en: Why الْعَمَلَ, with -a, after صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ?
why.a_en: أَنَّ, like إِنَّ, gives the noun after it -a: صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ الْعَمَلَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ مُرِيحٌ. The description keeps its -un.

selftest.why_en: مَعَ ذَلِكَ keeps your point after a concession, and فَنَّدَ is "refuted".
مُبَالَغَة is from بَالَغَ, to exaggerate.
وَجِيه is valid, worth taking seriously.

phrases_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ السَّفَرَ مُكْلِفٌ، وَمَعَ ذَلِكَ فَهُوَ يُعَلِّمُ الْكَثِيرَ
صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ الْعَمَلَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ مُرِيحٌ

lesson.arabic-supported-debate.title_en: A structured discussion: إِذَا فَهِمْتُكَ, بِنَاءً عَلَى, أَتَفَهَّمُ
lesson.arabic-supported-debate.family_en: Taking turns, showing you've listened, and basing your point on something
steps: In a structured discussion, each turn makes a claim, gives a reason or an example, or answers what was just said.
Show you've listened by restating the other view first: إِذَا فَهِمْتُكَ جَيِّدًا, if I've understood you.
أَتَفَهَّمُ, from the same root as أَفْهَمُ, acknowledges a view without agreeing with it.
Base your point on something: بِنَاءً عَلَى, based on, a source or a clearly labelled personal example.
Wait for your دَوْر, turn. If you must interrupt, ask first: هَلْ تَسْمَحُ لِي بِمُقَاطَعَتِكَ؟

examples.ar: إِذَا فَهِمْتُكَ جَيِّدًا، فَأَنْتَ تُفَضِّلُ الدِّرَاسَةَ وَحْدَكَ.
examples.en: If I've understood you, you prefer studying on your own.

examples.ar: بِنَاءً عَلَى تَجْرِبَتِي، الْمُرَاجَعَةُ الْيَوْمِيَّةُ أَنْفَعُ.
examples.en: Based on my experience, daily revision works better.
To sum up, each method has its advantages.

why.q_en: Why أَتَفَهَّمُ, and not just أَفْهَمُ?
why.a_en: أَفْهَمُ is "I understand" the words. أَتَفَهَّمُ, from the same root, is "I understand where you're coming from": it acknowledges a view, often just before you disagree.

selftest.why_en: A clarification is تَوْضِيح, and a summing-up خُلَاصَة.
بِنَاءً عَلَى تَجْرِبَتِي: based on my experience.

selftest.q_en: Which phrase restates the other person's view?
selftest.why_en: It checks you've understood before you answer.
